heroHeadline: NATO SWORD 26: 15,500 TROOPS DEPLOYED IN BALTIC — US FORCES EXERCISE WITH ALLIES TRUMP CALLS 'ABSOLUTELY USELESS'; AL JAZEERA: CAN EU ARTICLE 42.7 REPLACE NATO?; HEGSETH TO CONGRESS: EUROPE MUST TAKE 'PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY' FOR OWN DEFENSE
heroSubtitle: April 30 brings the starkest institutional paradox of the NATO-US crisis: as NATO's SWORD 26 exercise deploys 15,500 troops across the Eastern Flank and Arctic — including 6,000 US troops alongside partners from Estonia, Finland, Germany, Lithuania, Norway, Poland, and Sweden — President Trump continues to describe the alliance as 'absolutely useless' and having 'failed us.' The exercise, NATO's largest warfighting drill of 2026 and the first to integrate AI-enabled targeting systems, demonstrates that the institutional military alliance remains fully operational even as the political relationship between Washington and European capitals reaches a 77-year low. The same day, Al Jazeera published a major analytical piece asking whether the EU's Article 42.7 mutual defense clause — invoked only once, after the 2015 Paris attacks — could serve as a NATO substitute if the US commitment continues to erode: Macron has declared it 'in substance, stronger than Article 5'; Kallas warns that the EU blueprint is now operational; ambassador-level tabletop exercises are underway. On April 29, Defense Secretary Hegseth testified before the House Armed Services Committee, delivering what may be the most consequential US burden-sharing statement in decades: European allies must take 'primary responsibility' for Europe's conventional defense, with 'model allies' (Poland, Finland, Baltics) to receive preferential treatment and recalcitrant members to face consequences. Upcoming: Helsingborg NATO Foreign Ministers meeting (May 21–22); Ankara Summit (July 7–8).
